clue.text: Mountain ledge offering place of refreshment for one

indicators.note: the café stands for, or replaces, the 'one' inside the ledge word

parts.note: a sill is a narrow ledge below a window
the Roman numeral for one is I
a café is a place for a snack and a drink

explanation.surface: A climber spots a ledge high up that looks like a spot to stop for a cup of tea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for one' means CAFE takes the place of I in SILL, giving S-CAFE-LL; 'offering' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Proper name: Scafell is a peak in the Lake District, England's second-highest mountain.

clue.text: Church given warning signal — it may contain explosive

parts.note: amber is the traffic light warning drivers to get ready to stop

explanation.surface: A church receives a warning, perhaps about a bomb hidden inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A gun's firing compartment holds the cartridge and its propellant charge.

clue.text: Some careless officer found upside down in a ditch

indicators.note: in a down entry, turning the run upside down reads it from the bottom up, so backwards
only some of the letters of these two words are taken, a run spanning the gap

explanation.surface: An absent-minded officer has toppled head first into a ditch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some' takes ESSOF from carelESS OFficer; 'upside down' reverses it in this down light.
explanation.definitionFit: A fosse is a long trench or moat, especially one dug as a defence, so it is a kind of ditch.

clue.text: Bloater's not a bad sea food item

indicators.note: bad signals that the letters of the herring word, once the 'a' is gone, are spoilt into a new order

explanation.surface: A diner reckons a smoked herring is not a bad choice from the seafood menu.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not a' removes A from BLOATERS, leaving BLOTERS, which 'bad' rearranges. A bloater is a smoked herring.
explanation.definitionFit: This shellfish with big claws is a classic seafood dish served in restaurants.

clue.text: What Mussolini's supporters were to bring about

definitions.meaning: Mussolini was called Il Duce, so his backers were in favour of the Duce, written as two words

explanation.walkthrough: Mussolini's title was Il Duce ('the leader'), so his followers were PRO-DUCE. 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To cause something to happen or come into being; a synonym in the sense of generating results.

clue.text: Oxford martyr cleared with straight line laid down

parts.note: to be rid of something is to have cleared it away
a ley is a supposed straight line linking ancient sites across the landscape

explanation.surface: A martyr's name is cleared, and a straight line is drawn to mark it.
explanation.walkthrough: Ley lines are imagined straight alignments of ancient sites across the English countryside.
explanation.definitionFit: Nicholas Ridley, a Protestant bishop, was burned at the stake in Oxford in 1555, one of the Oxford Martyrs.

clue.text: Uneasiness I must hide in phoney rhapsody

indicators.note: the bigger group of letters has to conceal the single letter within it
something phoney is fake, so the letters of the music word are faked into a new order

explanation.surface: A listener feels uneasy at a fake piece of music and wants to hide from it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'phoney' rearranges RHAPSODY; 'must hide' puts I inside the result. 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A medical term for a state of general unease or dissatisfaction, the opposite of euphoria.

clue.text: Radical Argentinian university associated with a London club

parts.note: Che Guevara, the Argentine-born revolutionary
the LSE is the London School of Economics, part of the University of London

explanation.surface: A radical Argentine academic has ties with an exclusive London club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'associated with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Chelsea FC is a London football club based at Stamford Bridge.

clue.text: OAP leads conga, having worked out musical instruction

indicators.note: letters worked out are solved and put into a fresh order

explanation.surface: A pensioner leads the conga line, having first figured out the dance steps.
explanation.walkthrough: OAP (old-age pensioner) is a British term for a retired person.
explanation.definitionFit: Italian score marking telling players to go back to the sign and repeat from there.

clue.text: Animals run away, first to last

indicators.note: the opening letter of the word is moved round to the end

parts.note: scat is a command to an animal to go away quickly

explanation.surface: Animals bolt, the leader ending up at the rear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first to last' moves the S of SCAT to the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Pet felines are a common example of animals.

clue.text: Displays bowls of healthy breakfast food

parts.note: bran is a fibre-rich cereal eaten at breakfast
bowls are dishes

explanation.surface: A café puts out bowls of wholesome cereal for breakfast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of' is a link; the charade reverses the clue's order.
explanation.definitionFit: To wave something about for all to see, such as a weapon, is to show it off.

clue.text: One acted on making protest

definitions.meaning: in grammar, the noun that a verb's action is done to
to raise a complaint against something

explanation.walkthrough: 'making' is a link between the two senses.
explanation.definitionFit: In grammar the thing a verb acts on; as a verb, to raise a complaint or disagreement.

clue.text: Steamy and hot on the outside, turning purple

indicators.note: turning the letters over and around gives a new arrangement
only the outer letters of the word are taken

explanation.surface: Something steamy and hot on the surface starts to change colour to purple.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the outside' takes HT from hot; 'turning' rearranges STEAMY plus HT. 'and' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Amethyst is a violet quartz gem, and the name is used for its purple colour.

clue.text: Herald quiet about bad fellow, type falling short

parts.note: p (piano) is the musical marking for quiet
re means concerning, about
a cur is a contemptible man

indicators.note: falling short means the word comes up one letter shy, losing its end

parts.note: a sort is a type or kind

explanation.surface: A quiet herald talks about a scoundrel who doesn't measure up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'falling short' cuts the last letter of SORT.
explanation.definitionFit: A herald is a forerunner announcing what follows, which is what a precursor is.

clue.text: 150 workers end squatting inside — demanding types

indicators.note: squatters occupy the interior of a building, so this piece settles between the others

parts.note: CL is 150 in Roman numerals
worker ants are the classic crossword workers
an aim is an end or goal

explanation.surface: A hundred and fifty workers end up occupying a building, making demands.
explanation.definitionFit: People who claim something as their right are making demands for it.

clue.text: Nasty noise increased for listeners …

indicators.note: what listeners hear, not what is written, gives the letters

parts.note: something that has grown has increased in size

explanation.surface: An unpleasant noise is turned up louder for the audience.
explanation.definitionFit: A low cry of pain or displeasure is an unpleasant sound.

clue.text: … with this malfunctioning?

indicators.note: letters that are malfunctioning are out of order, so they are rearranged

parts.note: this points back to the previous answer, the nasty noise

explanation.surface: The ellipsis continues the previous clue: a nasty noise comes from something broken.
explanation.walkthrough: 'this' is the previous answer, GROAN, which 'malfunctioning' rearranges. A faulty church instrument does give a nasty noise.
explanation.definitionFit: A pipe or keyboard instrument that, when broken, wheezes out unpleasant moaning noises.

clue.text: Comedian given stick, loveless greeting

parts.note: a rod is a stick

indicators.note: love is zero in tennis, the letter O, and this word asks for it to be taken away

parts.note: hullo is a variant of hello

explanation.surface: A comedian is handed a stick and greeted coldly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loveless' drops O (love, nil in tennis) from HULLO. Rod Hull was a British TV entertainer famous for his puppet Emu.
explanation.definitionFit: Rod Hull was a British entertainer best known for his puppet act with the bird Emu.

clue.text: Magic hospital admitting deficiency

indicators.note: a hospital admitting a patient lets it in, so this piece goes inside

parts.note: Barts is St Bartholomew's, a famous London hospital
a lack is a deficiency

explanation.surface: A hospital admits it lacks resources, so perhaps it needs magic.
explanation.walkthrough: Barts is the usual name for St Bartholomew's Hospital in London.
explanation.definitionFit: Sorcery or witchcraft, especially the evil kind, is a form of magic.

clue.text: Historian's report of Cumbrian city

definitions.note: the 's stands for 'is', so the definition is just the historian, joined to the wordplay

indicators.note: a report is something heard, so the letters come from the sound

parts.note: Carlisle is the county town of Cumbria, in north-west England

explanation.surface: A historian writes an account of a northern English city.
explanation.walkthrough: Carlisle is a city in Cumbria near the Scottish border.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Carlyle was a Victorian Scottish writer whose works include a famous history of the French Revolution.

clue.text: What sounds like traditional office task in Asian town

indicators.note: what follows is to be heard rather than read

parts.note: typing letters was a standard office job

explanation.surface: Someone asks which old-fashioned clerical job is done in a town in Asia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'What' and 'in' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Taiping is a town in Perak, Malaysia, so an example of a town in Asia.

clue.text: Breasts shown by the old woman in old musical

indicators.note: in places the mother inside the title of the show

parts.note: Mame is a 1966 Broadway musical
ma, or the old woman, is an informal name for one's mother

explanation.surface: An actress playing a mother bares her chest in a vintage stage show.
explanation.walkthrough: Mame (1966) is a Broadway musical about an eccentric aunt; 'shown by' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The anatomical Latin plural for milk-producing glands in mammals.

clue.text: A mother with opportunity to get bargain non-alcoholic drink

parts.note: a dam is an animal's mother
a sale is an occasion to buy things cheaply

explanation.surface: A mother uses a chance at a bargain to buy a soft drink.
explanation.walkthrough: Adam's ale is old slang for water, since the first man had nothing else to drink. 'with' and 's' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Humorous name for plain water, a drink with no alcohol in it.

clue.text: Critic beginning to rattle American relations

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the next word is taken

parts.note: US for United States, American
kin are one's relatives

explanation.surface: A critic sets out to unsettle relations with the Americans.
explanation.definitionFit: John Ruskin was the leading Victorian writer on art and architecture, a famous critic.

clue.text: Tricky situation when energy's lacking in fight

indicators.note: lacking shows that this letter is missing from the larger word

parts.note: being in a scrape means being in a difficult spot
E is the abbreviation for energy, as in physics

explanation.surface: A tricky situation arises when a fighter runs out of energy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when' and 'in' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: A scrap is informal for a brawl or tussle.

clue.text: What could be seen as my one load of dubious cash?

parts.words: What could be seen as my one
parts.note: read as wordplay, the first part of the answer is an anagram signal and the second its fodder, which rearranges to the words 'my one'

explanation.surface: Someone asks what to make of a suspicious load of cash.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: 'funny' is an anagram signal, and its fodder rearranges to MY ONE. 'load of' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Counterfeit or illicitly gained currency, slang for cash of doubtful origin.

clue.text: Control what causes flooding, we say

indicators.note: spoken aloud, this signals the word is heard not read

parts.note: heavy rain causes floods

explanation.surface: We are told to manage the downpour that floods the land.
explanation.definitionFit: To rein in is to restrain or check, as with a horse's straps.

clue.text: Looking unwell, wanting disease got rid of

parts.note: flu, influenza, is a disease
shed means discarded

explanation.surface: A patient looks poorly and wants the disease gone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wanting' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A reddened, feverish face is a sign of illness.

clue.text: Maybe waste words introducing cross reference

definitions.meaning: leakage, such as liquid lost through cracks, is one kind of waste
an index tells readers to look at another sheet with a two-word note: see p.

explanation.walkthrough: The second sense splits as SEE PAGE, the phrase that sends a reader elsewhere in a book.
explanation.definitionFit: Slow leakage of fluid through porous material is liquid lost, a form of waste.
